AccessCertainty.description:
How the reported rights may differ from the truth, given what ADG has not seen.

Not a confidence score. Each value is a *direction*, derived from the conditions that
fired, and it is what lets a consumer tell a finding from a gap: rights reported
``AT_LEAST`` may be wider in reality, which means a risk rule reading them may be
looking at an under-count and must not conclude "nobody has access here".
AccessCertainty.title: AccessCertainty

AccessOutcome.description:
What the answer *is*, as one value a client can branch on.

The values are stable and appear in API responses; renaming one is a contract change.
AccessOutcome.title: AccessOutcome

AclEvaluationView.description: What one layer's ACL grants this token.

canonical_rights.description: What the canonical-ACL model would compute, for comparison.

entries_evaluated.description: Of those, how many named this token.
entries_evaluated.title: Entries Evaluated

order_dependent.description: True when the stored order changed this subject's answer: an Allow ahead of a Deny actually grants.
order_dependent.title: Order Dependent

owner_rights.description: Rights held by owning the object, outside the DACL. WRITE_DAC here is an escalation path no ACE shows.

superseded.description: Entries that matched and contributed nothing because an earlier entry had already settled every right they name.
superseded.title: Superseded

AclEvaluationView.title: AclEvaluationView

AclProvenance.description:
Where the DACL that was evaluated came from.

A projected DACL is a real answer — it is what Windows would have written on a cleanly
inheriting child — but it is a *prediction*, and a consumer that cannot tell it from a
reading of the object itself will eventually report one as the other.
AclProvenance.title: AclProvenance

AppliedAceView.description: One ACE that matched the token, and what it contributed where it sits.

access_mask.description: The entry's own mask, generic bits expanded.
access_mask.title: Access Mask

contributed.description: The part of the mask that survived what earlier entries had already settled. 0x00000000 means the entry is on the ACL and does nothing.
contributed.title: Contributed

layer.description: Which ACL this entry sits on: smb_share or ntfs. Carried on the entry itself so that a list drawn from both layers stays unambiguous — SMB 'Change' and NTFS 'Modify' are the same bits under two names.
layer.title: Layer

matched_key.description: The token entry this ACE named.
matched_key.title: Matched Key

position.description: Index in the DACL as stored. Order is load-bearing.
position.title: Position

AppliedAceView.title: AppliedAceView

BasisView.description:
The collected state an answer was computed from, as the contract renders it.

Every derived response carries one. It is what lets a client say *"as of the run that
finished at 02:14"* instead of *"as of now"*, and what lets two answers fetched minutes
apart be compared honestly: same token, same facts, and any difference between them is a
difference in the question rather than in the estate.

is_empty.description: True when no run has ever been recorded. Every derived answer over an empty estate reports no access, and here that means nobody looked.
is_empty.title: Is Empty

latest_activity_at.description: When a collector last wrote anything.
latest_activity_at.title: Latest Activity At

latest_run_id.description: The most recently updated run. Informational, not the key.
latest_run_id.title: Latest Run Id

token.description: The cache identity of the collected state. Equal tokens mean identical stored facts; this is the value the ETag is built from.
token.title: Token

BasisView.title: BasisView

CausalPathView.description: One route from the subject to one ACE on one object, and what it delivers.

ace_rights.description: The entry's own mask: what it is worth alone.

assumed.description: True when the ACE reached the subject through an assumed token SID (Everyone, Authenticated Users) rather than an observed membership.
assumed.title: Assumed

chain.description: The membership chain, subject first and ACL trustee last.
chain.title: Chain

constrained_rights.description: The part of layer_rights the other ACL withholds.

effect.description: What the path is worth. 'contributes' changed the final answer; 'redundant' means an earlier entry had already settled every right it names; 'constrained' means the other layer withholds all of it, so it does not affect access.

effective_rights.description: What it is worth to the final answer, after the layer crossing.

layer_rights.description: What it settled at its own layer that nothing earlier had already settled.

relation.description: Whether the ACE at the end allows or denies.

CausalPathView.title: CausalPathView

EdgeKind.description: What one edge in the explanation graph asserts.
EdgeKind.title: EdgeKind

EffectiveAccessView.description: The conclusion, with both layers and every qualification.

access.description: Whether any right survives. Read it with certainty: false with 'at_least' means no access was established, not that none exists.
access.title: Access

acl_provenance.description: Whether the NTFS DACL was read on this object, projected from an ancestor, or never seen.

limiting_layer.description: Which ACL removed rights the other granted. The field that says which ACL to go and fix.

EffectiveAccessView.title: EffectiveAccessView

ExplanationEdgeView.description: One edge of the explanation graph.

removable.description: Whether an administrator could actually delete this relationship. False for an assumed membership: there is no Everyone group to edit.
removable.title: Removable

ExplanationEdgeView.title: ExplanationEdgeView

ExplanationGraphView.description: The typed nodes and edges every path refers to, deduplicated.
ExplanationGraphView.title: ExplanationGraphView

ExplanationLimitsView.description: The bounds actually applied, after clamping.
ExplanationLimitsView.title: ExplanationLimitsView

ExplanationNodeView.description: One node of the explanation graph.

layer.description: ACE nodes only: which ACL it is on.
layer.title: Layer

position.description: ACE nodes only: index in the DACL as stored. Two entries naming one trustee are two nodes, because order decides which of them settles a right.
position.title: Position

ExplanationNodeView.title: ExplanationNodeView

FindingView.description: One thing the resolver assumed or could not settle.

may_overstate.description: True when this gap means the rights could be wider than reported.
may_overstate.title: May Overstate

may_understate.description: True when this gap means the rights could be narrower than reported.
may_understate.title: May Understate

FindingView.title: FindingView

LimitingLayer.description:
Which authorization layer removed rights the other would have granted.

The single most actionable field in a result: it sends an administrator to the ACL that
is actually in the way. "The user has Read" is a fact; "NTFS grants Modify and the share
grants Read" is a fix.
LimitingLayer.title: LimitingLayer

NodeKind.description:
What one node in the explanation graph is.

A principal and a group are distinguished because the *edge* between them means
different things to a reader: a user is where a chain starts, and a group is something
that can be emptied, renamed, or removed from an ACL.
NodeKind.title: NodeKind

PathEffect.description:
What a path is actually worth to the final answer.

The distinction this module exists to draw. All three describe an ACE that **matched
the token** — an ACE that names nobody in the token produces no path at all — and they
differ in whether that match changed anything.
PathEffect.title: PathEffect

PathRelation.description: Whether the ACE at the end of a path allows or denies.
PathRelation.title: PathRelation

PrincipalSummary.description: What is known about one principal, as far as any of it is known.

is_group.description: Null when the kind is unknown, never a guessed false.
is_group.title: Is Group

key.description: Storage key: the SID, or host|SID for a local group.
key.title: Key

kind.description: Null when no run has described this principal. The membership that reached it was still observed; only the description is missing.
kind.title: Kind

resolved.description: Whether ADG holds a principal record for this key.
resolved.title: Resolved

PrincipalSummary.title: PrincipalSummary

RemovalTargetView.description: What removing one edge would do, measured by re-running the access check.

alternate_paths.description: Contributing paths that still deliver rights afterwards.
alternate_paths.title: Alternate Paths

revokes_all_access.description: Whether removing this one edge leaves no rights at all. False while any alternate path survives.
revokes_all_access.title: Revokes All Access

rights_added.description: Effective rights *gained*. Non-empty means the edge carried a Deny and removing it would widen access.

rights_removed.description: Effective rights lost. Empty means removing this changes nothing, which is the honest answer whenever another path remains.

RemovalTargetView.title: RemovalTargetView

ResourceRef.description: Enough of a directory to identify it, with whether it was ever read.
ResourceRef.title: ResourceRef

RightsView.description: A rights mask, with its rendering alongside it. The mask is the answer.

categories.description: Every category the mask contains, strongest first.
categories.title: Categories

escalation_rights.description: WRITE_DAC / WRITE_OWNER, when present. The holder can self-grant.
escalation_rights.title: Escalation Rights

extra_rights.description: Rights present beyond what the categories cover.
extra_rights.title: Extra Rights

indeterminate.description: MAXIMUM_ALLOWED is present; Windows resolves it per open, so no fixed rights set exists.
indeterminate.title: Indeterminate

is_exact.description: False when the mask carries rights the label does not name.
is_exact.title: Is Exact

label.description: Display text derived from the mask. Never store or compare it: SMB 'Read' and NTFS 'Read & Execute' are the same bits, and 'Modify' can hide WRITE_DAC.
label.title: Label

layer.description: smb_share, ntfs, or effective. Masks never cross layers.
layer.title: Layer

mask.description: The access mask, as 0xNNNNNNNN. This is authoritative.
mask.title: Mask

primary.description: The strongest category the mask fully contains.
primary.title: Primary

unrecognized_bits.description: Mask bits matching no right ADG knows, as 0xNNNNNNNN.
unrecognized_bits.title: Unrecognized Bits

value.description: The same mask as an integer, for arithmetic.
value.title: Value

RightsView.title: RightsView

ShareRef.description: Enough of a share to identify it, with whether it was ever described.
ShareRef.title: ShareRef

TokenEntryView.description: One SID in the constructed access token, and why it is there.

depth.description: Membership hops from the subject. 0 for the subject itself.
depth.title: Depth

origin.description: subject, group_membership, well_known, or logon_type. The last two are assumptions, not observations.
origin.title: Origin

TokenEntryView.title: TokenEntryView

TokenView.description: The SIDs the ACLs were evaluated against.

membership_complete.description: False means the traversal hit a limit and the token is a lower bound.
membership_complete.title: Membership Complete

TokenView.title: TokenView

VerdictView.description:
The answer as one value, with the evidence that distinguishes it from its neighbors.

``access: false`` is two completely different findings and this is where they are told
apart. Branch on ``outcome``; render ``reason``; and never draw a negative conclusion
while ``conclusive`` is false.

certainty.description: Orthogonal to the outcome: the outcome is the verdict on the evidence, this is the direction the evidence can be wrong in. Both must be rendered.

conclusive.description: False only for 'indeterminate'. While false, 'this principal has no access' is not a statement this response supports.
conclusive.title: Conclusive

denials.description: Deny entries that actually withheld rights, both layers, in evaluation order. A projection of the per-layer 'denied_by' lists, placed here because it is the evidence for a 'denied' outcome. Entries that matched and took nothing away are not here; they are in the layer's 'superseded' list.
denials.title: Denials

may_understate.description: True when the real rights could be wider than reported — keep looking.
may_understate.title: May Understate

outcome.description: granted — rights survive. denied — none survive and a Deny entry is why. no_grant — none survive and nothing denied any; nothing names this principal. indeterminate — none were established and collection is incomplete in a direction that could hide a grant, so this is not a finding of no access.

reason.description: The operator-facing sentence for the outcome.
reason.title: Reason

VerdictView.title: VerdictView

description: The complete derivation of one principal's access to one directory: the verdict, both ACL layers, every causal path, and the measured effect of removing each edge. Returned by GET /api/v1/access/explain.

complete.description: False means the paths shown are a subset: at least one more route to these rights exists, so nothing may be concluded from the absence of one.
complete.title: Complete

cycles.description: Membership cycles in the traversed subgraph. A cycle is a finding.
cycles.title: Cycles

effective.description: The full derivation: the effective mask, and the NTFS and SMB evaluations that produced it with every contributing and denying entry.

paths.description: Every route from the subject to an entry that matched, with what each one is actually worth. Bounded, not paged; /api/v1/access/paths pages the same list when an estate produces more of them than one response should carry.
paths.title: Paths

removal_targets.description: Every removable edge on a path, with the measured effect of deleting it.
removal_targets.title: Removal Targets

schema_version.description: Version of the derived-answer contract this body conforms to. Additive changes bump the minor; a breaking change means a new major and a new path.
schema_version.title: Schema Version

warnings.description: Everything that qualifies this answer: assumptions made, trustees that could not be resolved, descriptors never read. The same list as effective.findings, surfaced here because it qualifies the whole response and not just the mask.
warnings.title: Warnings

title: AccessExplanationResponse
